subject.title: [Feature] Optionally forward session key to MCP servers via `params._meta` on tools/call

question: Should OpenClaw expose session identity to outbound MCP servers via a default-off tools/call _meta contract, and if so should that value be sessionKey, sessionId, channel/target metadata, or a narrower opaque caller id?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing to disclose session identifiers to MCP servers is a product and security boundary decision that affects config contract, privacy semantics, and overlap with existing caller-context work.

options.title: Approve narrow _meta forwarding
options.body: Add a per-server default-off option, document that the value is non-authoritative context, and cover stdio/HTTP behavior plus redaction and no-model-forgery tests.

options.title: Fold into caller-context design
options.body: Use the existing remote caller-context discussion as the canonical identity contract and decide there whether session identity belongs in headers, _meta, or a safer opaque field.

options.title: Decline sessionKey disclosure
options.body: Keep sessionKey private to OpenClaw and recommend server-local auth, per-session process isolation, or plugin-owned context instead of forwarding raw session identifiers.

recommendation.title: Fold into caller-context design
recommendation.body: Use the existing remote caller-context discussion as the canonical identity contract and decide there whether session identity belongs in headers, _meta, or a safer opaque field.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent MCP operator-control and config-surface history makes this the best available owner for the product/security contract choice.
